rationale: The Sloan-style balance-sheet accrual core is correctly constructed and the sign logic is coherent, but this is a measurement-robustness variant of the archive's AccrualsWhileSolvencyDeteriorates rather than a new hypothesis, so its value rests entirely on whether the −3.8%/yr alpha survives at much higher coverage.

Substituting retained-earnings erosion for leverage escalation is an economically distinct limb of the deterioration story (and captures loss-history firms that leverage ratios miss), giving a clean identifying contrast with the archive's leverage-trend result, though negative-RE firms may make the trend leg noisy.

The stated rationale is internally wrong — GROWTH(at) − GROWTH(dp) loads on asset growth with a coefficient of +1, so it does not purge the asset-growth confound at all and any negative slope is most plausibly a relabelled asset-growth (investment-factor) anomaly rather than evidence of stretched useful lives.

The flow-meets-flow liquidity channel is a legitimate and separable alternative to the leverage-trend conditioner, but the two legs are mechanically coupled through the cash-flow identity (a non-cash working-capital build is typically financed by falling cash), so the interaction risks behaving like a near-quadratic in accruals and the diagnosis will need that check.

Industry-demeaning accruals is a well-motivated purge of business-model variation that plausibly explains why the gen-1 level composites produced zero alpha, but it is a fairly standard adjustment applied to a design family that has already failed twice, so the prior on success is modest.

The maturity-mismatch funding channel is economically distinct from the level- and trend-of-leverage conditioners already tested, but note the mechanical coupling: because the accrual core adds back dlc, any increase in short-term debt inflates both legs simultaneously, so part of any result could be dlc growth interacted with itself.
